facts.statement: P1 EdgeRest PostureUp (ASIN B0CN8VC121) is a single-piece L-shaped black pad, 24 x 3.5 x 1 in, memory-foam core, low-friction woven PU/cotton cover, textured non-slip underside rated for wood, glass and laminate; the listing is sold under a variation parent (B0F1HVV9CC) that also offers a 16 x 3 in 'Mini'. Title on amazon.com: 'EdgeRest PostureUp L-Shaped Desk Long Wrist Rest Elbow, Forearm & Wrist Comfort Support for Table or Desk Edge, Non-Slip, Memory Foam Padding, Ergonomic Design for Work, Universal Fit, Black'.

EdgeRest (B0CN8VC121) shows 4.6 stars with 226 ratings on the Amazon Australia storefront and 4.6 stars with 204 ratings on Amazon UK (search snippets, 2026-10-06); one unattributed snippet shows 4.5 stars. The amazon.com count itself was not captured, so 226 is the largest confirmed count for this ASIN.

On the brand's own store the EdgeRest standard (24 in) is priced $59.99 marked down from $69.99 and the EdgeRest Mini (16 in) $47.99; the brand site carries a 4.85-star average from 27 reviews and says the cushion was designed by a Doctor of Physical Therapy. The amazon.com shelf price was not visible in any snippet.

Review snippets for EdgeRest praise foam that is firm enough to support without flattening, a pad that stays put on the desk, and a profile thin enough not to get in the way; no sliding or smell complaints surfaced in two searches, and no 1-2 star review text was retrievable (all review pages egress-blocked).

P2 ArmCloud (ASIN B0FHMXYL7G, sold by the Arm Cloud Store) is a single extra-long L-shaped pad that hugs the desk edge, 28 x 3.5 x 1.2 in, memory foam with a breathable Lycra cover carrying carved grooves over a polyurethane layer, anti-skid rubber base with no adhesive; first available 15 July 2025. The listing title has been changed between 'ArmCloud Desk Edge Rest, Memory Foam Keyboard Wrist Rest, Long Ergonomic Elbow & Forearm Support...' and 'Desk Edge Cushion, Extra Long 28 Inch Arm Rest Pad for Desk, Memory Foam'.

ArmCloud's price, star rating and review count did not appear in any snippet across three searches (Amazon, Amazon India mirror, ReviewMeta, camelcamelcamel and the eBay cross-listing 188204575476 are all egress-blocked for fetching); the product is confirmed to exist on Amazon and eBay but its numbers are unverified.

P3 JIKIOU L-Shaped Desk Elbow Pad 2 Pack, black (ASIN B0FH22782P) is listed at $17.99 with 4.4 stars and 791 ratings; each pad is 14.9 x 3.5 x 0.6 in, cloth cover over slow-rebound memory foam with a 'massage' texture, rubber base plus 6 removable adhesive pieces (one snippet says 12 adhesive strips) to lock it to the desk.

JIKIOU runs the same L-shaped 2-pack in pattern/colour variants: Black Flowers (B0FYFMKBK5), Marble Pink (B0FYFVLD6H) and a 'Leather' cloud-print White (B0G5NLY1M5); an older snippet of the black listing gives 15.75 x 3.94 in as the size, so the pad length is somewhere between 14.9 and 15.75 in.

Amazon results for 'elbow pad desk' show a wave of near-identical L-shaped 2-pack listings, all with 2025-2026 ASIN prefixes: MEKASS diamond black 2 pcs (B0F28ZPFCV), Sushret 2-pack (B0FJ5RR8JK), Vaydeer 2Pcs L-Shaped (B0FNMMJ2RQ), MOSISO diamond 2 pcs (B0GCMKR1JH), ELZO 2-pack (B0FW4QSD93), Tiiyee separate-design (B0FNMVCC8K), an unbranded 24 in full-size rail (B0FCCZ2B14), an adjustable-spacing 2-pack (B0G482W69W) and a 2-in-1 pad-plus-mousepad set (B0GS5MVFLP). Prices and ratings for these were not in the snippets.

Unbranded L-shaped memory-foam 2-piece desk-edge pads are cross-listed on Walmart and eBay; a search summary across those listings put consumer prices at roughly $16.98 at the low end up to $69.99 (the EdgeRest regular price) at the top.

Carried over from the 2026-09-23 category run: VAYDEER's Upgraded Larger and Thicker Elbow Rest Pad (single L-shaped memory-foam pad, about 7.37 x 5.07 x 0.94 in) sells at $17.99 with 4.6 stars and 2,045 reviews, the largest review count found on any page-one elbow/forearm desk pad.

Carried over from the 2026-09-23 category run: first-page prices for 'elbow rest pad for desk' span about $8 (small gel pads) to $20+ (large foam pads or clamp-on trays), with simple cushioned pads clustering at $13-17 and a median near $15.50.

Carried over from the 2026-09-23 run: Leolee memory-foam elbow pads (non-slip base, 1- and 2-packs) draw praise for relief but some buyers still feel the hard desk through the pad, pointing to insufficient foam depth or density (complaint cluster C1).

Carried over from the 2026-09-23 run: Jelbows gel elbow pad set (2-pack, about $16.49, 1,100+ reviews) has as its commonest complaints the surface turning sticky over time and a plastic smell (complaint cluster C2).

Carried over from the 2026-09-23 run: Fuzadel clamp-on elbow trays (about $20) draw complaints that the cushion is thin and the desk-clamp connector feels unstable (complaint cluster C3, base/mount fails).

A retailer blog on new-wrist-rest odour attributes it to VOC off-gassing from PU foam and coated fabrics, typically fading over 3-14 days; this is the mechanism behind the 'smells like plastic' complaints in cluster C2.
Carried over from the 2026-09-23 run: Amazon's referral fee for the Office Products category is 15% of the sale price with a $0.30 per-item minimum, unchanged for 2026.

2026 US FBA fulfilment fees (effective 15 Jan 2026, non-apparel, $10-$50 price band) fetched this run: small standard 2 oz $3.32, 4-6 oz $3.45, 8-10 oz $3.68, 14-16 oz $3.96; large standard up to 4 oz $3.73, 4-8 oz $3.95, 12-16 oz $4.60, 3-20 lb $6.97 plus $0.08 per 4 oz; a 3.5% fuel and logistics surcharge is added to every fulfilment fee from 17 April 2026. The 10-12 oz small-standard row and the 1-1.5 lb large-standard row were not in the snippet (sellerguards.com carried the same table).

Carried over from the 2026-09-23 run: Amazon's 2026 fee notice raises small-standard fulfilment fees by $0.12/unit for items under $10 from 15 Jan 2026 and adds a 3.5% fuel surcharge from 17 April 2026.

CBP ruling NY N216783 classified a polyurethane-gel palm/wrist rest pad with a vinyl top layer under HTSUS 8473.30.5100 (parts and accessories of automatic data-processing machines, other) at a FREE general rate of duty; no ruling specific to a desk-edge elbow/forearm pad was found.

CBP classifies polyurethane foam sheet from China under 3921.13.5000 at 4.2% ad valorem; a search summary also cited a memory-foam neck pillow with a knit polyester cover classified 9404.90.2000 with the Section 301 List 4A line 9903.88.15 (7.5%) applied, which is the fallback family if a fabric-covered desk pad is treated as a cushion rather than a computer accessory.

Carried over from the 2026-09-23 run: the Penn Wharton Budget Model put China's effective US tariff rate at about 33.9% as of January 2026 (2.3% a year earlier), stacking MFN duty, Section 301 tranches (7.5% List 4A to 25% Lists 1-3) and the 2025 IEEPA/reciprocal layers; the tranche for this product's subheading was not confirmed.

Sourcing: an Alibaba wholesale listing 'L-Shaped Desk Edge Ergonomic Support Memory Foam Elbow Pad Arm Rest for Palm Wrist Forearm Non-Slip Separate Design' is priced at $3.20 per piece with a 50-piece minimum order; the snippet does not say whether a 'piece' is one pad or the 2-pad separate-design set, and no logo or retail packaging is included at that price. The same results page lists an 'Arm Rest Rectangular Memory Foam Elbow Pads Non-Slip Base 300x100x30mm' item (a close match to the founder's 300 x 100 x 20 mm spec) without a price in the snippet, and MOQs on the page range from 2 to 300 pieces.

Sourcing: Alibaba's 'office elbow pads' showroom shows memory-foam armrest/elbow pads from $3.09 per unit with a minimum order of 1 piece (sample-tier pricing, 1-pc, no logo or packaging stated); bulk tiers and foam density are not visible in the snippet.

Founder's supplier quote, reference only, no public URL (recorded from brief.json assumptions, contact 'Ahmad'): EXW USD 7.58 per piece as a single, about USD 5.75 per 2-piece set without logo (genius should confirm whether 5.75 is per set or per piece in the set configuration, since it is below the single-piece price), mould USD 230, MOQ 300 pcs; sample spec L-shaped foldable memory-foam pad, milk-silk fabric cover, 300 x 100 x 20 mm, about 250 g per piece, kraft mailer 32 x 11 x 6.5 cm per 2-pc set (590 g/set), 30 sets per 58 x 34 x 43 cm carton.

price_ladder.anchor_note: Anchored on the single-piece L-shaped lip pad. The first row is dominated by 2-pack short L-shaped pads at $16.98-17.99 (JIKIOU $17.99 F7, unbranded 2-packs from $16.98 F10, VAYDEER's upgraded single pad $17.99 F11), so the visual anchor is about $17.50 — a little above the $15.50 broad-term median carried over from the 2026-09-23 run (F12). The $8 floor is small gel pads (F12). The long single-rail form (EdgeRest $59.99 on the brand site, F3; ArmCloud price unknown, F6) sits 3x above the anchor and reads as a different mental category. The founder's $15-25 band therefore spans 0.86x to 1.4x the anchor: up to about $22.70 passes the 1.3x gate silently, $23-25 needs a visible reason in the thumbnail.

variant_chosen.description: Single-piece L-shaped 'lip' memory-foam pad: one foam profile whose front lip folds over the desk's front edge so the forearm never meets the edge, fabric cover (lycra, cloth or milk-silk), rubber or adhesive-dot non-slip base, black. It is sold in two pack forms — a pair of short pads of about 12-16 in each (JIKIOU, MEKASS, Sushret, MOSISO, Vaydeer 2Pcs, and the founder's planned 300 x 100 x 20 mm 2-pc set) or one long 24-28 in rail (EdgeRest, ArmCloud). Every price, rating, review count and complaint in this file is anchored on the L-shaped single-piece pad; where the pack form matters it is stated on the row.
variant_chosen.why: All three focus products share the L-shaped lip geometry, so it is the shape the buyer compares. Among them the 2-pack short-pad form carries the most social proof at the founder's price band (JIKIOU 791 ratings at $17.99, F7, versus EdgeRest's 204-226 at roughly $60, F2/F3), and the 2025-26 look-alike wave on page one is almost entirely 2-pack short pads (F9). The 2,045-review VAYDEER pad (F11) is a single L-shaped pad at the same $17.99, confirming the price point. The long-rail form sells at 3x the price with fewer reviews.

complaint_clusters.pattern: Pad is too thin or too firm; the buyer can still feel the hard desk edge through it after an hour.
complaint_clusters.root_cause_hypothesis: Share carried over from the 2026-09-23 run (Leolee, F13); not re-measured on the focus products because no 1-2 star text was retrievable. The focus grid's thickness ladder makes the exposure visible: JIKIOU 0.6 in (F7) versus EdgeRest 1.0 in (F1) and ArmCloud 1.2 in (F5) — the cheap 2-pack form is the thin one, and the founder's 20 mm (0.79 in) sits between.
paraphrased_examples: Still feel the desk edge pressing through the pad.

complaint_clusters.pattern: The cover or gel surface turns sticky and smells of plastic after a few weeks of skin contact.
complaint_clusters.root_cause_hypothesis: Share carried over from the 2026-09-23 run (Jelbows, F14). Mechanism: VOC off-gassing from PU foam and PU-coated fabric, then breakdown under skin oil and heat (F16). Lycra/PU covers (ArmCloud, F5) and cloth covers (JIKIOU, F7) are both exposed; EdgeRest advertises a low-friction woven surface that wipes clean (F1).
paraphrased_examples: Started smelling like plastic after a few weeks.

complaint_clusters.pattern: The pad creeps or slides off the edge; the base or mount does not hold on the real desk.
complaint_clusters.root_cause_hypothesis: Share carried over from the 2026-09-23 run (Fuzadel clamp, F15). On the L-shaped form the signal is that JIKIOU ships 6-12 removable adhesive pieces on top of its rubber base (F7) — the base alone is not trusted to hold — while EdgeRest and ArmCloud sell a textured or anti-skid rubber underside with no adhesive (F1, F5).
paraphrased_examples: Clamp connector felt wobbly and cheap.

praise_clusters.pattern: Noticeable relief from elbow and forearm soreness or pins-and-needles within days of regular use during long typing or gaming sessions (carried over from the 2026-09-23 run).
The pad stays put on the desk through active mousing and chair movement, so the buyer forgets it is there.
Foam is firm enough to support without flattening and the profile is low enough not to get in the way of the keyboard (EdgeRest snippets, F4).

referral_rate.assumption: Carried over from the 2026-09-23 run (F17): flat 15% Office Products referral rate for 2026; the high end reflects the $0.30 per-item minimum, which is irrelevant inside the $15-25 band but kept for a sub-$10 clearance price.

fba_fee_usd.assumption: Fetched this run (F18). Low = small-standard 8-10 oz row at the $10-50 band ($3.68) for one 250 g pad shipped flat as a single — only valid if the 20 mm pad compresses under the small-standard thickness limit, which was not fetched; verify. Base/high = the founder's actual SKU, a 2-pc set at 590 g (1.3 lb) in a 32 x 11 x 6.5 cm mailer, which is large standard 1-1.5 lb: that row was not in the snippet, so it is interpolated between the fetched $4.60 (12-16 oz) and $6.97 (3 lb) rows, then the 3.5% fuel surcharge (from 17 Apr 2026) is added; high also covers the set being measured into the 1.5-2 lb band.

storage_per_cuft_month_usd.assumption: Not fetched this run (search budget spent on the three focus products and sourcing); carried over as stale from the 2026-09-23 run, which used previously published Amazon standard-size rates of about $0.78/cu ft Jan-Sep and $2.40/cu ft Oct-Dec. duty_rate.assumption: Fetched this run (F20, F21). Base assumes the pad classifies like the ruled PU palm/wrist rest under 8473.30.5100 at a free general rate (the listings call themselves keyboard wrist rests). sea_freight_usd_per_cbm.assumption: Not fetched this run; carried over as stale from the 2026-09-23 run (general China to US West Coast LCL market range). The founder's carton is 58 x 34 x 43 cm = 0.085 cbm for 30 sets, so even the high end is small per set; still get a live forwarder quote.

additional_tariff_rate.assumption: Carried over as stale from the 2026-09-23 run (F22). Low = Section 301 List 4A 7.5% plus a 10% reciprocal layer; base = the roughly 30-34% non-MFN stack implied by the 33.9% effective China rate reported for January 2026; high = a 25% List 1-3 tranche plus IEEPA and reciprocal layers if 8473.30 falls in an early list. The exact tranche for the final subheading was not re-fetched; widened by a quarter as the standard requires.

unanswered_questions: Does the L-shaped lip actually fit a thick (over 1 in) or rounded/bullnose desk edge, and how far does the lip hang down? Recurring across the category Q&A; every listing shows a thin square edge only — a missing dimensioned diagram image.
Does a 1-1.2 in pad lift the forearm above a low-profile keyboard and bend the wrist up? The long-rail listings (EdgeRest 1.0 in, ArmCloud 1.2 in) never show the pad next to a keyboard in profile.
Two short pads or one long rail: can a 2-pack be spaced for keyboard plus mouse without a gap at the elbow? Nobody shows the spacing in a top-down image.
Does the rubber base hold on glass or glossy laminate without the adhesive strips JIKIOU ships — a missing 'works on five desk surfaces' proof image.
Can the cover be removed and washed, or only wiped? No listing shows a care step.
Will it work on the left side for a left-handed mouse user (carried over from the 2026-09-23 run).
trends: In the twelve months to October 2026 the L-shaped lip pad became the default form on page one: ArmCloud launched 15 July 2025 (F5) and JIKIOU, MEKASS, Sushret, Vaydeer 2Pcs, MOSISO, ELZO and Tiiyee all carry 2025-26 ASIN prefixes (F9) — a clone wave is already in progress, and the differentiation has moved to surface pattern (diamond quilt, 'massage' texture, cloud/marble/leather prints) and colour variants (F8).

A premium long-rail rung opened above the 2-pack cluster: EdgeRest at about $60 on its own site (F3) and ArmCloud at 28 in (F5) sell one 24-28 in piece instead of two short pads, at roughly 3x the $17.50 anchor.
Carried over from the 2026-09-23 run: demand shifted from small gel discs toward larger L-shaped foam pads (VAYDEER's large pad holds 3-4x the reviews of its smaller variants, F11).
Amazon's 2026 FBA fee table plus the 3.5% fuel surcharge from 17 April 2026 (F18, F19) adds roughly $0.15-0.20 per unit on this size tier, compressing margin at the $15-20 price point.
